reason: If the cache dir can't be written, the stamp is never created. list-status.sh:147 (`mkdir -p ... || true`) and :168 (`printf ... >"$_autosync_ts" 2>/dev/null || true`) swallow the failure, so _autosync_last stays 0 (:150) and the spawn at :169-178 runs on every render. The fast path never helps either, because segment-cache.sh:124 `[[ -f "$ts" ]] || return 1` sends each render to the full cold path. The code path is real. It is graded down from high because the trigger is uncommon: the Claude Code statusline subprocess normally has a writable $HOME/.cache, and Codex has no statusline surface. When it does fire, it multiplies the unlocked overlapping-sync race in status-4.
fix: Spawn only if the stamp write succeeded: `if printf '%s\n' "$_autosync_now" >"$_autosync_ts" 2>/dev/null; then (spawn); fi`. That also skips autosync when the cache dir is unwritable. Minimal and correct.

reason: Only one global stamp exists. list-status.sh:146 and segment-cache.sh:123 both build `<cache>/segment-autosync-ts` with no ledger component, while the segment cache itself is keyed per ledger (segment-cache.sh:45-47). With the 3-5 parallel repos that are normal here, each 600 s window syncs only the repo whose render crosses the boundary first. SessionStart and PostToolUse still sync each repo, so counts don't go stale forever, but autosync's stated purpose (picking up external merges mid-session) is lost for every repo but one. Canonical item of the autosync cluster (status-2 / status-3 / ledger-9). status-3 is a different root cause in the same mechanism.
fix: Key the stamp per ledger using the same sanitized name: `<cache>/segment-autosync/$name`. Change it in both list-status.sh:146 and segment-cache.sh:123 together, or the fast path will read a stamp the slow path never writes. Pairs with the status-1 fix.

reason: cmd_status finds the ledger from `${cwd:-${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-$PWD}}` (list-status.sh:99), but the spawned `"$0" sync` (:177) inherits PWD, and sync resolves its ledger from PWD only (sync.sh:61 `fi_find_issues_file` with no argument; parse-entries.sh:23 defaults to $PWD). The installed templates usually hide this by cd-ing first (statusline-target.sh:201, statusline-install.sh:423), and the bash-target template also falls back to CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR. The mismatch is still reachable in two cases: the canonical inline/append templates' no-jq branch (statusline-install.sh:425 and the append twin), which runs with no cd while CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR is set, and a manual `status --cwd X` run from elsewhere. The global stamp is consumed either way. Different root cause from status-2, grouped with it per the brief.
fix: Spawn as `( cd "$search_root" 2>/dev/null && FOUND_ISSUES_AUTO_ARCHIVE=off "$0" sync ... & )`, and the same for FOUND_ISSUES_AUTOSYNC_CMD. Use search_root, not `${file%/*}`: it mirrors cmd_status's own resolution exactly and keeps git/gh in the right repo.

reason: sync reads the whole ledger in a loop (sync.sh:100-361) that calls `gh pr view` with no timeout (:139, :156), then writes the result back with `mv "$tmp" "$file"` (:367). There is no lock and no re-check before the write. rg finds no flock or lock dir anywhere in lib/bin/hooks. Any mutating command that rewrites the ledger during the gh loop is silently overwritten. Autosync (list-status.sh:177) makes this recurrent and unattended. The comment at :133-136 only considers two syncs racing, not lost updates. Same root cause as ledger-1 / annot-6.
fix: Add a per-ledger mkdir lock with a stale-pid check, shared by sync and every mutating command. Minimal interim step: capture the ledger content or mtime before the loop and abort the mv if it changed. Also wrap gh in a timeout.

reason: For `console.log("x");` the Node installer (statusline-target.sh:548) emits `" + __fiSeg(typeof dir...:(typeof cwd...:undefined)));  // found-issues:seg`. The uninstall regex at statusline-uninstall.sh:106/119 needs `[^)]*\)\s*\);`, but after the first two `)` comes a third `)` where it expects `;`, and :107/:120 can't match either. The Python plain form (statusline-target.sh:785) emits `+ _fi_seg(locals().get("dir") or ...))`, which defeats :113/:114 at `locals()`. The block that defines __fiSeg/_fi_seg is still removed (:94-98), so the leftover call throws ReferenceError/NameError while :131 prints success. Tests only cover the template-literal and f-string forms (tests/cli-install-statusline-custom-target.bats:267, :336). Graded medium: the statusline goes blank after an explicit uninstall, but the session itself keeps working.
fix: Call fi_strip_target_markers (the literal strip_lit surgery, statusline-core.sh:295) on the target after detecting language from the extension. Add the missing Python concat literal ` + _fi_seg(locals().get("dir") or locals().get("cwd"))` to it: its regex fallback at statusline-core.sh:375 fails on `locals()` the same way, so the v1.5.x migration path has this bug too. Add tests for plain console.log and print("x").

reason: The awk at statusline-uninstall.sh:51-53 (and the custom-target version at :94-98) sets skip at the start marker and clears it only on an exact end-marker line, so a missing or edited end marker drops everything to EOF. Neither uninstall path takes a backup. The install path calls cmd_uninstall_statusline with no backup on installed-broken (statusline-install.sh:122), while backups only happen at :139/:160. One correction to the finder: when only the end marker is missing and the block is current, fi_statusline_state reads to EOF, finds __FI_DIR and --cwd (statusline-core.sh:121-127), and returns installed-fixed, a no-op. So install truncates only for an old (pre---cwd) block. Explicit `uninstall-statusline` truncates in every case.
fix: In both awk passes, count start and end markers first and refuse (non-zero exit with a message) when they are unbalanced. Call fi_save_statusline_backup before any in-place rewrite, including uninstall.

reason: `mv "$tmp_atomic" "$path"` (statusline-target.sh:352, :574, :811) replaces a symlink with a regular file, so the `[[ -L "$path" ]]` warning checked afterwards (:360, :581, :818) can never fire. The canonical paths also mv over the link with no check at all (statusline-uninstall.sh:56, :128; statusline-install.sh:434). Meanwhile the append path uses `>>` (statusline-install.sh:450), which follows the link, so behaviour is inconsistent. A symlinked ~/.claude statusline into a dotfiles/agent-config repo is a realistic setup here.
fix: Resolve the real path once at the top of each install/uninstall (portable readlink loop, since macOS readlink has no -f) and operate on it. Or test -L before the mv and warn/refuse there. Moving the existing warning above the mv is the minimum.

reason: --dry-run and --apply only set target_mode (statusline-install.sh:52-59), and target_mode is read only inside the --target branch (:74-77). Without --target, execution falls through to the canonical mutating logic (:97-195): the inline insert, the append, and the installed-broken uninstall-plus-reinstall. No test covers `install-statusline --dry-run` without --target (rg finds none).
fix: Reject --dry-run, --apply and --language without --target, using exit 2 and a usage line. That is the smallest safe change. Honouring --dry-run in the canonical path can come later.

reason: Pass is declared on `-n "$probe_output" && probe_has_error -eq 0` (statusline-install.sh:274) without checking that the found-issues segment appears in the output, so any host output counts as 'Segment rendered'. On the FAIL branch, sub-probe (a) at :285 greps for ' \| ' and misreports a clean ledger as 'binary resolution / cwd'. Downgraded to low: it's a doctor diagnostic, not a hot path, and the static splice-gap check (:297+) partly compensates.
fix: Compute the expected segment with `found-issues status --format=segment --cwd "$probe_cwd"`. If it is non-empty, require it as a substring of probe_output. If it is empty, report 'ledger clean, nothing to render' instead of pass or fail.

reason: statusline-install.sh:213 takes awk `$NF` and expands only `${HOME}` and a leading `~`, so quotes and an unbraced `$HOME` survive, and paths containing spaces split. `-f` then fails and :223-229 silently probes $FI_STATUSLINE_FILE instead of the configured script.
fix: Strip surrounding quotes, expand both `$HOME` and `${HOME}`, and when the configured path is set but isn't a file, print a warning naming it rather than switching targets silently.

reason: fi_find_bash_splice_point prints every matching line number (statusline-target.sh:124 for LINE1=, :127 for echo), and the awk splices every line in splice_set (:296-314). Two consecutive LINE1 assignments both get `${__FI_SEG}`, so the segment renders twice. With no LINE1, every echo is spliced. For `echo x >&2` the unquoted `${__FI_SEG}` lands in the redirect word (an 'ambiguous redirect' once the segment holds spaces), and for `echo "$x" | jq -r '.a'` it is appended to jq's filter. The canonical installer, by contrast, uses only the last LINE1.
fix: Splice only the last LINE1 assignment, or the last echo/printf when there is no LINE1. Skip candidates containing a redirect or pipe. If several candidates remain, exit 16 (the unused multiple_splices code) instead of guessing.

reason: The append install is chosen whenever there are fewer than 2 LINE1 assignments (statusline-install.sh:191-194). cmd_install_statusline_append (:446-492) appends after a trailing newline check and never scans for a top-level exit/exec, so a block placed after `exit 0` never runs while install reports success. status-9's probe then shows a false pass.
fix: Before appending, look for a top-level `exit`/`exec` line (unindented) after the last output statement and insert the block above it, or refuse with a message.

reason: fi_count_in_pr (parse-entries.sh:375-376) and fi_count_residual (:412) grep the whole entry line for `(PR: o/r#N)`. fi_parse_entry, and therefore sync, only honours the trailing annotation run (fi_annotation_tail :60-69; rationale at :192-197). A PR mentioned mid-line is counted 'in PR' even though sync will never close the entry. The demoted grep in fi_count_stale (~:460) has the same whole-line looseness for `(PR-closed:|commit-stale:`.
fix: Count in_pr, residual and demoted from the annotation tail. In awk: strip trailing recognized `(key: ...)` groups into a tail string and match against that. Ideally this lands in the single-pass counter proposed in status-14.

reason: total_open is computed on every call (list-status.sh:116) but used only in the json branch (:184-185). critical, in_pr, residual and stale each re-run fi_entries plus grep pipelines (:115-123), and fi_count_stale forks date and runs a second fi_entries pass. fi_find_issues_file forks `$(cd && pwd)` (parse-entries.sh:25) plus `$(dirname)` per directory level (:36). The segment cache absorbs most warm renders on bash 4.2 and later.
fix: Guard total_open behind `[[ $format == json ]]`. Add one awk pass that prints all counts, with the cutoff computed once. Replace `$(dirname "$dir")` with `${dir%/*}` and a `/` guard, as the fast path already does (segment-cache.sh:113-114).

reason: Both bin/found-issues:51 and fi_segment_cache_key (segment-cache.sh:42) require fi_segment_clock_ok, i.e. bash 4.2 or later (:35-37), so under macOS /bin/bash 3.2 every render takes the full cold path plus the autosync mkdir, date and stat (list-status.sh:147-158). This is a documented design limit (segment-cache.sh:23), not a correctness bug. It is a real cost on a stated target platform whenever the statusline resolves to /bin/bash.
fix: For bash below 4.2, get now and today from one `date +%s:%Y-%m-%d` fork, then use the same content-checked cache compare. One fork replaces about 35.

reason: fi_capture_mode (statusline-core.sh:38-40) tries BSD `stat -f '%Lp'` first. Under GNU stat (Linux and Git Bash), `-f` means filesystem mode, where %L is not a valid directive. The repo already documents the same trap for `stat -f %m` succeeding with garbage (list-status.sh:152-155, detect-mode.sh:35-39). If the call exits 0 with garbage, `chmod "$mode"` fails. The installers then fall back to `chmod +x`, giving 0700/0711 instead of the original mode, and the custom-target uninstall (statusline-uninstall.sh:129, `|| true` with no fallback) leaves the file at mktemp's 0600 with no execute bit. Existing tests only assert -x (tests/cli-statusline.bats:273, :289), which the fallback satisfies.
fix: Try `stat -c '%a'` first, validate `^[0-7]{3,4}$`, then try BSD with the same validation, then fall back to 755.
repro: On Linux: `touch f; chmod 644 f; stat -f '%Lp' f; echo rc=$?` (expect garbage such as `?p` with rc=0). Then install and uninstall --target on a 0755 .sh statusline and run `stat -c %a` on it after each step.

reason: bin/found-issues:29 sets `set -euo pipefail`. A bare `--target` dereferences an unset `$2` at statusline-install.sh:41 and statusline-uninstall.sh:24, which aborts with 'unbound variable' and no usage text. `--target --apply` takes '--apply' as the path and fails with 'does not exist' (exit 12).
fix: In both parsers: `[[ $# -ge 2 && $2 != --* ]] || { fi_err '--target requires a path'; return 2; }`.
